newsitem.title: UK: British DTI company investigations at record level.
newsitem.headline: British DTI company investigations at record level.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said that it started a record 411 company investigations during 1995-96 with 390 completed.
The DTI said in a report published on Monday that it had considered 1,341 cases for investigation.

The main type of alleged misconduct was theft, which rose to 143 in 1995-96 from 93 cases in 1994-95, and alleged management of the company by an undischarged bankrupt, or disqualified, director which was up to 76 cases from 44.
The DTI said a record total of 912 directors were disqualified in 1995-96.
Of these, 727 were disqualified following the failure of their companies, while 191 were disqualified after being convicted of company related offences.
Twenty eight cases of possible insider-dealing were referred to the DTI by the Stock Exchange for consideration compared with 13 in the previous year.
Offences of failing to file annual returns and accounts led to the conviction of 636 directors, said the DTI.
